questions.question: In this project, what does `generateStaticParams` on the `[slug]` post page do?
options: Validates the slug format at runtime
Pre-renders a page for every post slug at build time instead of on first request
Generates TypeScript types for the params object
questions.explanation: It returns the full list of slugs ahead of time so Next.js can statically generate a page per post at build time.

questions.question: After `postComment` runs, why does it call `revalidateTag("posts")` instead of just returning success?
options: revalidateTag is required syntax for every Server Action
It invalidates every cached fetch tagged 'posts', so the post page and listing page both show the new comment/updated data
It has no functional effect, only logging
questions.explanation: Without revalidating, the Data Cache would keep serving the pre-comment version of the post and listing pages.

questions.question: Why does `CommentForm` use `useActionState` instead of calling `postComment` directly in an onClick handler?
options: useActionState is required for all functions
It bridges the Server Action into the Client Component, giving pending/error UI state while the mutation still runs on the server
It replaces the need for a form element
It caches the comment locally instead of submitting it
questions.explanation: useActionState wires a Server Action's result and pending status into component state, without needing a hand-written fetch call or loading-state management.

questions.question: Why is `generateMetadata` used on the post page instead of a static `metadata` export?
options: Static metadata isn't supported in the app router
The title and description depend on the fetched post, which is only known once the post's data is loaded per slug
It's required whenever generateStaticParams is used
questions.explanation: Since each post has a different title/excerpt, the metadata must be computed dynamically per slug rather than hardcoded once.
